mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% indicates economic weakness that reduces corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 1.0% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3.0%, the economy is in a 'sweet spot' of expansion without overheating, supporting positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL < 3.0%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, strong industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, serving as a leading indicator of economic expansion that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth is positive in more than 50% of cases but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 0.5% and consumer credit (RSAFS) expands by more than 0.3%, robust household spending momentum drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and RSAFS growth > 0.3%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0%), the central bank's policy shift to reduce liquidity suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
